subject: Next steps & technical plan for NorthStar inference pilot
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Murray <alex.murray@northstar.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: NorthStar pilot — summary & immediate next steps

Alex — thanks again for the 45-minute call today. Quick recap from our side and the next actions we agreed on:

Summary of pain & goals
- Current inference pain: unpredictable p95 latency spikes during peak batch scoring (customer-facing suggestions) leading to degraded UX.
- Desired SLO: p95 <= 150 ms for single-turn text generation for core product flows; tail latency budget for complex prompts up to 400 ms.
- Throughput targets: baseline 500 QPS with burst capacity to ~1,000 QPS for scheduled marketing spikes.
- Model needs: instruction-tuned LLM for summarization + reranking. You indicated preference for an open model (Llama2-13B family or FLAN-like alternative).
- Security: SOC2 and VPC options required for production.

What Redwood recommends (high level)
- Run a dedicated pilot on Redwood Dedicated in us-west to validate latency + cost trade-offs.
- Start with a quantized Llama2-13B variant (4-bit / q4) for the pilot; fall back to a float16 flavor for tail-critical flows.
- Employ KV-cache warmup + prefix caching for frequent templates to cut per-request compute on average by ~25-35%.
- Canary plan: 10% traffic -> 30% -> 100% with real-time latency dashboards in Redwood Console and automatic fallback to a lower-capacity variant under strain.

Immediate next steps (agreed)
1) Technical workshop for detailed capacity modeling (Karthik + Marissa + your infra) — target next Tue/Wed.
2) You to share a 48‑hour production-like traffic sample (anonymized request timestamps, avg tokens in/out, and success/error codes).
3) Redwood to send a preliminary capacity model + pilot cost estimate and a draft SLA for review (attached).

Attachments: preliminary SLA (northstar-sla-draft.pdf) and the mutual action plan template.

If that matches your recollection, we'll lock the workshop time.

Thanks,
Sean

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Murray <alex.murray@northstar.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: NorthStar pilot — technical options & trade-offs

Alex / team — adding some concrete topology options and assumptions so we can hit the workshop prepared. Notes below are targeted at the 500 QPS baseline with 1k burst and the p95 <= 150 ms target.

Assumptions
- Typical prompt length: 60 tokens in, expecting ~120 tokens out for generation flows; reranking calls average 10 in / 20 out. (If your distribution is different please send sample.)
- Preferred deployment region: us-west (low-cost path with proximity to your users).

Option A — Dedicated GPU pool (recommended for predictable latency)
- Topology: 4 x A100 (80GB) in a reserved pool + 2x warm standbys for burst; autoscale policy to add 2x A100s at 70% avg utilization.
- Model: quantized Llama2-13B (q4f16 or q4_0) — expects p95 ~110–160 ms for 120-token outputs with continuous batching disabled for tail-critical routes.
- Throughput estimate: ~500–800 single-request QPS depending on batching; batching increases throughput but raises tail latency.
- Pros: predictable p95, strong isolation. Cons: higher fixed cost.

Option B — Multi-variant routing (cost-aware fallback)
- Topology: primary pool with quantized 13B + warm float16 7B variants.
- Routing policy: latency-first for customer-facing routes; cost-first for background jobs. Automatic fallback to 7B when queueing > 100 ms.
- Expected p95: primary ~130 ms; fallback ~90 ms for short prompts but lower quality on complex instruction tasks.

Optimization levers (what moves the needle)
- KV / prefix caching: warm KV cache for repeated users reduces compute by ~30% on average.
- Dynamic batching: use small-window batching (5–10 ms) for internal async jobs, disable for sync customer requests.
- Quantization: 4-bit gives major cost wins; validate quality with a prompt set (we'll run A/B evals in the pilot).

Pilot plan items for workshop
- Collect 48h traffic sample + 1 week of peak-hour traces.
- Run local capacity sweep with your anonymized sample to generate a capacity table (I attached ns-capacity-modeling.csv).
- Define canary thresholds and SLO rollback policies.

Questions for you before the workshop
1) Do you require streaming token-by-token responses for the UX? That changes latency expectations slightly.
2) Any upper bound on acceptable model-quality drop if we route to smaller variants during overload?
3) Who owns procurement (PO timing) if we move to Reserved Dedicated capacity?

I'll bring a sample capacity spreadsheet and a short simulation during the workshop.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Alex Murray <alex.murray@northstar.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: NorthStar pilot — technical options & trade-offs

Thanks Sean / Karthik — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from our side:

1) Token distribution: our production requests average ~45 tokens in and ~90 tokens out for suggestion flows; reranking calls are roughly as you estimated. We'll export the 48h sample and strip PII.
2) Streaming: yes — we need streaming for the frontend suggestions to render progressively (so p95 should account for time-to-first-token).
3) Quality tolerance: product team prefers routing to smaller variants only for non-critical background tasks; for direct user suggestions we want to avoid quality regression beyond a small human-observable threshold.
4) Procurement timeline: procurement can sign a PO in ~4 weeks pending SOC2 and SLA terms.

Workshop: Wed Aug 19 works for us (10:00 PT). Please share an invite. Also please include a preliminary cost delta ballpark in the pilot doc — we need a rough number for our finance lead.

Alex
